annotations.description: Temple of Deceit provides a free Scry 1 on entry, which is valuable card selection especially on Turn 1. All three lands enter tapped, so there's no tempo difference, but the scry from Temple of Deceit is pure upside that was passed up. Mistvault Bridge's indestructible quality is rarely relevant.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Mistvault Bridge as the Turn 1 land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Temple of Deceit to get the free Scry 1, saving Mistvault Bridge and Bojuka Bog for later turns.

annotations.description: Playing High Market (colorless land) on Turn 1 over Island delays access to colored mana. Island should generally be played first to enable casting colored spells as early as possible, while High Market can be played later when its colorless-only production is less constraining.
annotations.actionTaken: Played High Market as the Turn 1 land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Island first to have blue mana available for early spells, save High Market for a later turn

annotations.description: Playing Selesnya Sanctuary on turn 1 means bouncing a land back to hand (or itself if no other lands), resulting in having 0 lands on the battlefield after the bounce. This effectively wastes turn 1 entirely since the Sanctuary enters tapped and requires bouncing a land. Playing Island or Plains first would provide immediate mana access on turn 2, and Selesnya Sanctuary could be played on turn 2 to bounce the basic land back while still having had mana available.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Selesnya Sanctuary on turn 1 with no other lands in play, resulting in bouncing itself or having no untapped mana and losing tempo.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island or Plains on turn 1, then play Selesnya Sanctuary on turn 2 bouncing the basic land back. This gives the same mana development but allows potential turn 1 plays and better sequencing.

annotations.description: Casting Lightning Greaves on turn 1 with only 0 cards in hand (after drawing) and no creatures means paying 2 mana for an equipment that does nothing yet. More importantly, the player should play a land first before casting spells. They have Island, Swamp, and Simic Growth Chamber available as land drops. Playing a land first is fundamental sequencing - you always want to make your land drop before casting spells to ensure you don't forget it. Additionally, with 0 mana available on turn 1, casting a 2-mana artifact shouldn't even be possible unless lands were already played. The sequencing of casting before land drop is the key issue here.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Lightning Greaves before playing a land on turn 1
annotations.betterLine: Play a land first (Island or Swamp), then if enough mana is available, consider casting Lightning Greaves or save mana for future turns

annotations.description: Player stated they need green mana for Troll Ascetic (1GG) but played Island which only produces blue. With 0 cards in hand, the tempo loss of Simic Growth Chamber entering tapped is minimal, and it would provide green mana that Island cannot.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Island, which produces only blue mana
annotations.betterLine: Play Simic Growth Chamber, which produces both green and blue mana, directly supporting the stated goal of casting Troll Ascetic. With an empty hand, the enters-tapped downside is negligible.

annotations.description: On turn 1 with {G/W}{G/W} Selesnya Guildmage available to cast (using hybrid mana, Plains can pay for both symbols), playing Island instead of Plains means the Guildmage cannot be cast this turn or next turn without a green/white source. Plains would enable casting the 2/2 creature on turn 2 with another land, or even potentially this turn if another white/green source were available. Island provides blue mana but there are no blue spells mentioned in hand, making it a less useful land drop on turn 1.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Island as the turn 1 land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Plains to enable casting Selesnya Guildmage on turn 2 (with a second G/W land). Island doesn't contribute to any castable spell in hand.

annotations.description: Playing Bojuka Bog on turn 1 is suboptimal because it enters tapped and produces only black mana, which doesn't cast any of the cards in hand (all requiring white, blue, or colorless). Skycloud Expanse also enters tapped but produces white or blue mana, which is far more relevant for casting Steel Overseer on turn 2 (or other spells). Bojuka Bog's graveyard exile ability is essentially worthless on turn 1 when no opponent has cards in their graveyard yet. Playing Skycloud Expanse instead would set up a turn 2 Steel Overseer, which is the ideal curve play.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Bojuka Bog as the turn 1 land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Skycloud Expanse to have access to white or blue mana on turn 2, enabling Steel Overseer or Sanwell on curve

annotations.description: On turn 1 with what appears to be a full mana base (all 5 cards are castable options), Steel Overseer at 2 mana is a more efficient play that comes down earlier and begins accumulating value by pumping artifact creatures. Digsite Engineer costs 3 mana and its token-generating ability requires casting artifact spells afterward. Playing Steel Overseer first means it can start buffing any artifact creatures played on subsequent turns, including the Constructs that Digsite Engineer would later create. The sequencing of Steel Overseer into Digsite Engineer on the following turn is stronger than the reverse, as the Overseer can immediately start pumping any tokens Digsite Engineer creates.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Digsite Engineer for 3 mana
annotations.betterLine: Cast Steel Overseer for 2 mana, saving 1 mana and setting up to pump future artifact creatures including Digsite Engineer's Construct tokens

annotations.description: Kaseto (2/2) was chosen over Trygon Predator (2/3 flying with artifact/enchantment removal on combat damage). Trygon Predator has a better body, built-in evasion, and generates value without additional mana investment. Kaseto requires {G}{U} each activation and has lower toughness.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Kaseto, Orochi Archmage (2/2) on Turn 1
annotations.betterLine: Cast Trygon Predator (2/3 flying) - better stats, evasion, and free value on combat damage without needing additional mana each turn

annotations.description: Playing Simic Growth Chamber on turn 1 with no other lands in play means bouncing nothing (or bouncing itself if it's the only land, which effectively wastes the turn). However, the bigger issue is that Simic Growth Chamber enters tapped and bounces a land, so on turn 1 it sets the player back - they'll have 0 untapped lands and need to replay a basic land next turn, effectively losing a turn of development. Playing Swamp would allow casting Fleshbag Marauder on turn 3 more reliably, as the bounce land on turn 1 delays mana development. With a hand containing a 3-drop (Fleshbag Marauder) and a 7-drop (Slipstream Eel), getting to 3 mana quickly is important.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Simic Growth Chamber as the first land drop, which enters tapped and bounces a land (likely itself or nothing if it's the only land).
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp to have an untapped mana source immediately, saving Simic Growth Chamber for a later turn when there's a basic land to bounce and replaying it won't cost tempo.

annotations.description: On Turn 1, playing a basic Island when Temple of Deceit was available. If the player has no 1-mana plays, Temple of Deceit would provide a free scry while still being untapped by Turn 2, making it strictly better sequencing.
annotations.actionTaken: Played basic Island on Turn 1
annotations.betterLine: Play Temple of Deceit on Turn 1 to get a free scry 1, saving the basic Island for a turn where entering untapped matters more. This depends on whether they had a 1-mana play in hand.

annotations.description: Cast Steel Overseer before playing Skycloud Expanse. Fundamental sequencing dictates playing your land first before casting spells - it preserves maximum options and provides more information before committing mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Steel Overseer for {2} before playing a land
annotations.betterLine: Play Skycloud Expanse first, then cast Steel Overseer

annotations.description: Cast a spell before playing an available land (Skycloud Expanse). Generally you should play lands before casting spells to maximize available mana and options. Additionally, on turn 1 it's unclear if they even have the mana to cast a {1}{W} spell without playing Skycloud Expanse first.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Sanwell, Avenger Ace ({1}{W}) without first playing Skycloud Expanse
annotations.betterLine: Play Skycloud Expanse first, then cast a 2-mana creature if mana permits

annotations.description: Caller of the Claw's ETB trigger creates Bear tokens for each nontoken creature that went to your graveyard this turn. On turn 1, no creatures have died, so the ETB trigger creates zero tokens — it's just a 2/2 for 3 mana with flash that gained no value from its ability. Kaseto, Orochi Archmage is a 2/2 legendary creature for 3 mana (1GU) that has a repeatable activated ability making creatures unblockable (and pumping Snakes), providing ongoing value. Kaseto is clearly the stronger turn 1 play as it provides a relevant ability for future turns, whereas Caller of the Claw's flash and ETB ability are wasted when cast proactively with no deaths.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Caller of the Claw on turn 1 with no creatures having died, getting a vanilla 2/2 for 3 mana.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Kaseto, Orochi Archmage instead, which provides the same 2/2 body but with a powerful repeatable activated ability for future turns.

annotations.description: Caller of the Claw has significant upside in multiplayer as a flash response to board wipes, creating multiple 2/2 bears. Noble Quarry (1/1 lure for 3, or 6 mana bestow) is arguably a weaker card to keep, as the lure effect often gets your creature killed in multiplayer without accomplishing much.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Caller of the Claw
annotations.betterLine: Discard Noble Quarry instead, as Caller of the Claw's flash wrath-insurance is more valuable in multiplayer than a fragile lure creature

annotations.description: One with the Machine draws cards equal to the highest mana value among artifacts you control. With Steel Overseer (CMC 2) likely being the only/main artifact on board, this draws only 2 cards for 4 mana - an inefficient use. More importantly, the player has 0 cards in hand according to the board state, meaning these are likely the only cards available. Casting Tawnos, Solemn Survivor (a 1/3 for 2 mana) would develop the board and leave mana open, while Steel Overseer is already on board providing value. Tawnos could also increase the CMC ceiling for a later One with the Machine cast. Playing the draw spell now with only a CMC-2 artifact means getting minimal value from it.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast One with the Machine for 4 mana, likely drawing only 2 cards (based on Steel Overseer's CMC of 2).
annotations.betterLine: Cast Tawnos, Solemn Survivor for 2 mana to develop the board, then activate Steel Overseer. Save One with the Machine for when you have higher-CMC artifacts in play to draw more cards, or at minimum cast Tawnos first so you have a CMC-2 creature and could potentially play other artifacts before using One with the Machine.

annotations.description: Attacking with Steel Overseer means it cannot tap to put +1/+1 counters on artifact creatures. Steel Overseer is a 1/1 whose primary value comes from its activated ability, not from dealing 1 damage in combat. Tapping it to pump artifact creatures (including itself and potentially Sanwell if Sanwell is an artifact) would generate more value over time than attacking for 1. Additionally, a 1/1 is very vulnerable in combat and could easily be blocked and killed.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with both Steel Overseer and Sanwell, Avenger Ace.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with only Sanwell, Avenger Ace (3/1) and keep Steel Overseer back to use its tap ability to put +1/+1 counters on artifact creatures during second main phase or on future turns.

annotations.description: Steel Overseer is far more valuable as a tap ability engine that pumps all artifact creatures with +1/+1 counters each turn than as a 1/1 attacker. Attacking with it risks losing it in combat for just 1 damage, while keeping it back allows accumulating counters on all artifact creatures over multiple turns, which generates significantly more value.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Steel Overseer as a 1/1 alongside Sanwell, Avenger Ace.
annotations.betterLine: Keep Steel Overseer back to use its tap ability to put +1/+1 counters on artifact creatures, growing the board incrementally rather than risking it in combat for minimal damage.

annotations.description: Caller of the Claw's value comes from its flash ability and its ETB trigger creating Bear tokens based on nontoken creatures that died this turn. On Turn 1, no creatures have died, so the ETB trigger creates zero tokens — it's just a vanilla 2/2 for 3 mana. Meanwhile, Trygon Predator is a 2/3 flyer for the same cost that can destroy artifacts/enchantments on combat damage, and Kaseto is a legendary 2/2 that provides an unblockable activation. Wistful Selkie is a 2/2 that draws a card on ETB. All of these provide significantly more value than a vanilla 2/2.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Caller of the Claw on Turn 1 with no creatures having died, getting a vanilla 2/2 for 3 mana.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Wistful Selkie (2/2 that draws a card), Trygon Predator (2/3 flyer with artifact/enchantment destruction), or Kaseto (useful activated ability) — all provide substantially more value for similar mana cost.

annotations.description: Caller of the Claw on turn 1 with no creatures having died this turn produces no Bear tokens - it's just a 2/2 for 3 mana with flash that gains no value from its ETB ability. Meanwhile, Kaseto, Orochi Archmage or Trygon Predator are both 2-power creatures for the same mana cost but with relevant ongoing abilities. Trygon Predator (2/3 flying with artifact/enchantment destruction on combat damage) provides a better body and evasion, and Kaseto provides an unblockable activation. Caller of the Claw's value is as a reactive flash creature after a board wipe, not as a proactive turn 1 play.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Caller of the Claw as a vanilla 2/2 with no ETB value
annotations.betterLine: Cast Trygon Predator (2/3 flying with relevant combat damage trigger) or Kaseto, Orochi Archmage (repeatable unblockable ability) for the same mana cost

annotations.description: Caller of the Claw on turn 1 with no creatures having died this turn creates no Bear tokens - it's just a 2/2 for 3 mana with flash. Noble Quarry is only a 1/1 for the same cost, so Caller is the bigger body. However, Caller of the Claw's value is entirely in its ETB trigger which is wasted here with no creatures in the graveyard. Noble Quarry at least has a relevant ability (lure effect) that could matter in combat later, and its bestow mode gives it late-game utility. That said, a 2/2 body is generally better than a 1/1 body on an empty board, so this is defensible.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Caller of the Claw as a vanilla 2/2, wasting its flash ETB trigger
annotations.betterLine: Could argue Noble Quarry is better since its abilities have future relevance, while Caller's trigger is completely wasted. However, the 2/2 vs 1/1 body difference makes this debatable.

annotations.description: Discarded Tawnos, Solemn Survivor to Syphon Mind, which is likely a key value engine in an artifact deck. If Tawnos is not their commander, this loses a high-value repeatable effect. Swiftfoot Boots is generally a lower-impact card that would be a safer discard.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Tawnos, Solemn Survivor to Syphon Mind
annotations.betterLine: Discard Swiftfoot Boots instead, as it's a replaceable equipment piece, while Tawnos provides ongoing value generation in artifact strategies. If Tawnos is their commander (goes to command zone), then the discard is actually optimal.

annotations.description: Caller of the Claw is a highly situational card that only generates value when your nontoken creatures have died this turn. In a general card selection, more consistently powerful cards were available.

annotations.betterLine: Select Trygon Predator (evasive 2/3 flyer with artifact/enchantment removal on combat damage) or Kaseto, Orochi Archmage (repeatable unblockable ability) as they provide consistent value without requiring specific board states.

annotations.description: With 0 cards in hand and likely unused mana available, declining to activate Troll Ascetic's regenerate ability ({1}{G}) wastes mana that could provide a free protective shield until end of turn. This is a pure-upside activation when there's nothing else to spend mana on.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Troll Ascetic's regenerate ability.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Troll Ascetic's regenerate for {1}{G} to put a regeneration shield on it as insurance against any destruction effects, since the mana would otherwise go unused.

annotations.description: The player has 0 cards in hand and is choosing to cast Slipstream Eel for 7 mana. While the game says it's castable, the board context is unusual - it's Turn 1 and they have 0 cards in hand, which suggests something abnormal about the game state. More importantly, they have the option to activate Troll Ascetic's regeneration ability, which could be relevant for protection. However, casting a 6/6 creature is generally a strong play if the mana is available. The reasoning given is theatrical rather than strategic, and trusting 'the system's assessment' without verifying mana availability or considering whether to hold up regeneration mana for Troll Ascetic is somewhat questionable. If the Troll Ascetic is in play and might face removal, keeping {1}{G} open for regeneration could matter, but deploying a 6/6 is a significant board presence addition.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Slipstream Eel (6/6 for 7 mana) instead of activating Troll Ascetic's regeneration
annotations.betterLine: Casting Slipstream Eel is likely correct as deploying a 6/6 threat is high impact, but the player should have considered whether they needed to hold mana for Troll Ascetic's regeneration ability if removal was likely.

annotations.description: On Turn 1, Gem25P Timmy activated Rubinia Soulsinger before playing their land for the turn. They have Rupture Spire in hand which they could play first. Rupture Spire enters tapped and requires paying {1} when it enters, so they need mana available to pay for it. By tapping Rubinia first (and presumably using their Island for mana considerations), they are potentially missing their land drop or missequencing. More importantly, it's Turn 1 and they should be focused on developing their mana base rather than activating Rubinia. Playing Rupture Spire as their land drop should be the priority since missing land drops in the early game is very costly. Additionally, activating Rubinia to steal a creature means Rubinia stays tapped, and if Rupture Spire needs {1} paid on ETB, they may not have the mana to keep it.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Rubinia Soulsinger instead of playing Rupture Spire as their land drop first.
annotations.betterLine: Play Rupture Spire first (making the land drop), then consider activating Rubinia Soulsinger if mana permits. Sequencing lands before spells/abilities is fundamental, especially early game when developing mana is critical.

annotations.description: Rubinia Soulsinger is a much more powerful card in a multiplayer game, offering repeatable creature theft which is extremely strong. Steel Overseer is only good when you have multiple artifact creatures to buff, and without knowing the rest of the deck composition, its value is speculative. Rubinia Soulsinger provides a powerful political tool and removal effect that scales well in multiplayer.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Steel Overseer (1/1 artifact creature that puts +1/+1 counters on artifact creatures)
annotations.betterLine: Rubinia Soulsinger is likely the strongest pick here as a repeatable Control Magic effect in multiplayer, though without full deck context Steel Overseer could be defensible if the deck is artifact-heavy.

annotations.description: On Turn 1, the player activated the Simic Growth Chamber / Drake Roost ability on their Island, which costs {G}{U} and tapping the land. On turn 1, they would only have 1 land (the Island they just played), which produces {U} with its first ability. They cannot pay {G}{U} with a single Island - they don't have the mana to activate this ability. Even if somehow the game allowed it, spending all mana on turn 1 to create a 2/2 flyer while tapping your only land is questionable. But the fundamental issue is they chose an ability they cannot pay for.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated the {G}{U}, {T} ability to create a 2/2 Drake token, which requires {G}{U} mana they don't have on turn 1 with only an Island.
annotations.betterLine: Tap Island for {U} mana using the {T}: Add {U} ability, or simply pass if there's nothing to cast.

annotations.description: Llama4 Rivals has 0 cards in hand and is using basic landcycling on Ash Barrens, which requires paying {1} and discarding the card. With 0 cards in hand after this activation, they're spending mana to search for a basic land instead of just playing Ash Barrens as a land (which produces colorless mana). On turn 1, playing Ash Barrens as a land is almost always better since it gives you a land on the battlefield immediately for free, whereas landcycling costs {1} mana (which they may not have) and only puts the land in hand, not on the battlefield. Additionally, with 0 cards in hand, getting a land into hand rather than onto the battlefield is strictly worse tempo.
annotations.actionTaken: Used basic landcycling on Ash Barrens to search for a basic land card and put it into hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Ash Barrens as a land to have it on the battlefield immediately, preserving tempo on turn 1.

annotations.description: Caller of the Claw's ETB trigger creates Bear tokens for each nontoken creature that died this turn. On turn 1, no creatures have died, so the ETB is wasted — it's just a 2/2 for 3 mana with flash that gains no value. Kaseto, Orochi Archmage is a 2/2 legendary creature for 3 mana with a relevant repeatable activated ability that can make creatures unblockable (and pump Snakes). Wistful Selkie is a 2/2 that draws a card on ETB. Either of those would provide more value than a vanilla 2/2.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Caller of the Claw as a 2/2 with no ETB value on turn 1.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Wistful Selkie to get a 2/2 body plus draw a card, or cast Kaseto for its repeatable unblockable ability. Caller of the Claw should be saved for a turn when creatures have actually died to maximize its token generation.

annotations.description: Caller of the Claw's value comes from its ETB trigger creating Bear tokens for each nontoken creature that died this turn. Kaseto, Orochi Archmage is a 2/2 for 3 mana with a relevant activated ability that can make creatures unblockable (and pump Snakes), providing much more utility throughout the game. Caller of the Claw would be better held for a reactive flash play after a board wipe or removal.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Caller of the Claw on turn 1 as a vanilla 2/2 with no ETB value.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Kaseto, Orochi Archmage instead for the same stats but with a useful repeatable unblockable ability, saving Caller of the Claw for a later reactive flash play when creatures have died.

annotations.description: On Turn 1, Gem25P Timmy activated Steel Overseer (tapping it to put +1/+1 counters on artifact creatures) instead of playing a land. Steel Overseer is the only artifact creature on the board, so it only puts a +1/+1 counter on itself - making it a 2/2. While this isn't terrible, the player should have played a land first (Seaside Citadel or Rupture Spire) before activating Steel Overseer. Playing a land costs nothing and develops mana, and you can still activate Steel Overseer afterward. Missing a land drop on turn 1 is a real cost - it delays mana development. Additionally, Seaside Citadel enters tapped so playing it now (when you can't use the mana anyway) is the most efficient time.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Steel Overseer to put a +1/+1 counter on itself without playing a land first.
annotations.betterLine: Play Seaside Citadel (enters tapped, so best played early when you can't use the mana immediately), then activate Steel Overseer.

annotations.description: Wrexial is a 5/8 and Sanwell is a 3/1. Blocking with Wrexial would kill Sanwell (a relevant creature with abilities) while Wrexial takes only 3 damage and survives as a 5/5. There is no risk to Wrexial and it removes an attacker permanently. Taking 3 damage for no reason when you have a free, risk-free block available is a clear mistake. Troll Ascetic could also block and kill Sanwell, though it would die in the process (3/2 vs 3/1 - both die). Wrexial blocking is strictly better as it survives.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose not to block Sanwell, Avenger Ace (3/1), taking 3 damage unnecessarily.
annotations.betterLine: Block Sanwell with Wrexial, the Risen Deep (5/8). Wrexial kills Sanwell and survives at 5/5, preventing 3 damage and removing an opponent's creature for free.

annotations.description: Relic Crush costs {4}{G} and the player has 0 cards in hand - this card is being cast from hand with no hand. More importantly, Relic Crush destroys up to one artifact and up to one enchantment - it cannot target creatures like Baleful Strix. The reasoning mentions targeting Baleful Strix which is a creature, not an artifact or enchantment (though Baleful Strix is actually an artifact creature, so it could be a valid target). However, the key issue is that this is being cast during combat when attacking GPT52 Villain, but the targets mentioned (Azorius Signet, Baleful Strix) belong to Llama4 Rivals. Casting a 5-mana spell during combat to destroy permanents belonging to a player you're not even attacking is questionable at best. Furthermore, the player has 0 cards in hand, so casting this uses all their mana during combat when they could instead hold up mana for Troll Ascetic's regeneration ability ({1}{G}) to protect it. The Troll Ascetic regeneration activation was the other option and would be far more valuable for protecting their attacking creature.

annotations.betterLine: Activate Troll Ascetic's regeneration ability to protect it during combat, or save mana for defensive purposes. Relic Crush could be cast post-combat if targets are truly valuable.

annotations.description: Blocking a Drake Token (2/2 flyer) with Vedalken Humiliator (3/4) is fine in terms of surviving combat, but Thought Monitor (2/2) could also block and trade with the 2/2 Drake Token. Vedalken Humiliator is a much more valuable creature (3/4 with a powerful metalcraft ability) than Thought Monitor. Using the Humiliator to block a mere token preserves the less valuable creature while risking the more valuable one unnecessarily. While the Humiliator survives the block (3/4 vs 2/2), so no creature is lost, the choice is still reasonable. However, if there were any combat tricks possible, the Humiliator would be the bigger loss. Since the Humiliator survives at 3/2 remaining toughness, this is fine - no creature is lost either way.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Drake Token with Vedalken Humiliator (3/4)
annotations.betterLine: Block with Thought Monitor (2/2) to trade the less valuable creature with the token, preserving the more powerful Vedalken Humiliator at full health. Though Humiliator survives the block too, trading away the Thought Monitor (which already drew cards on ETB) is generally preferable to taking damage on the Humiliator.

annotations.description: The player had Steel Overseer's activated ability available ({T}: Put a +1/+1 counter on each artifact creature you control) and chose to cast Liquimetal Torque instead. The reasoning mentions targeting Scythe Specter to make it an artifact and references attacks that don't match the board state, suggesting confused/hallucinated reasoning. More importantly, activating Steel Overseer to pump artifact creatures is generally a high-priority free action that should be done, especially since the mana for Liquimetal Torque could still be spent afterward (or Steel Overseer could have been tapped first). Without seeing the full board, the sequencing of casting Liquimetal Torque before activating Steel Overseer means the Overseer's counters won't count the Torque as an artifact creature (it's not a creature), but the confused reasoning and potentially suboptimal sequencing represent a minor error.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Liquimetal Torque with confused reasoning about targeting Scythe Specter and referencing nonexistent attacks.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Steel Overseer first to put +1/+1 counters on all artifact creatures, then cast Liquimetal Torque with remaining mana if applicable.
